comment: NTT command files (main.txt / main.cfg): one chat command per line. HAND-MAINTAINED - unlike syntaxes/ntgml.tmLanguage.json and syntaxes/ntgml-legacy.tmLanguage.json this file is not written by tools/generate-grammar.ts, and there is nothing to regenerate. SOURCES, in decreasing authority. (1) The NTT 100.034 data.win, which is what the game actually dispatches: 122 command names, being every `chat_cmd_<name>` script in its string pool (the dispatcher builds that script name from the typed word - the literal `chat_cmd_` sits just past the table) plus every alias registered in its `/help` table at byte offsets 1492476-1495280, less the nine argument labels that share the region (code framerate milliseconds mode object seconds value variable where). (2) The NTT FAQ chat-command list (NTT-FAQ.dmd in YellowAfterlife's bits-of-nuclear-throne, which is not part of the api/ntt-docs copy vendored here), 49 names, every one of them confirmed by the binary. (3) NTGML-SPEC.md section 9, whose names the binary also all confirms; the ones the FAQ does not list are allowmod gml2 loadarea loadcfg loaddir loadloc loadskill loadtxt sideload - the FAQ does document /loadtext and /loadconf, inside its /load entry. (4) The local corpus, 25 `main*.txt` under `mods/` plus an empty `main.txt` at the game root, where /load /loadmod /loadwep /loadskin /loadrace /loadcrown /loadskill /loadtext /timeout /allowmod /unloadmod were seen in real use. THREE THINGS THIS GRAMMAR ASSUMES, none of them documented anywhere. Commands are matched in lower case only, so `/LoadMod` is flagged: no source says whether the dispatcher folds case, but every tabled, documented and observed name is lower case. `//` line comments are not described by NTT anywhere; they are inferred from shipped files (mods/vagabonds/main.txt, `mods/vagabonds/custom options/main.txt`) and from NTGML-SPEC.md section 9. Leading whitespace is tolerated on purpose, to keep the highlighter lenient, although no corpus line is indented and nothing says the game strips it. A non-blank line that is neither a comment nor a slash command is left unscoped - what the game does with such a line is not documented.
name: NTT command file

comment.comment: A whole-line comment. `//loadmod x` - no space after the slashes - is how a line is disabled, so this must win over every command rule.
comment.name: comment.line.double-slash.ntt-main

timeout-seconds.comment: The network timeout, in seconds. Integer or decimal is an assumption: the FAQ says only "Time is in seconds" and the binary "[number of seconds]", and `/timeout 600` is the only form anyone has been observed to write.

timeout-invalid.comment: Anything else after /timeout is not a duration. Must follow #timeout-seconds.

gml-command.comment: The argument is one line of NTGML. It is scoped as embedded GML but the ntgml grammars are deliberately NOT included: they carry begin/end rules (block comments, strings, macro continuations), and an unterminated one - `/gml /* x` - would push a rule stack that swallowed every following line of the command file. Nothing in this format spans lines, so every rule here is a single-line match.

bare-command.comment: Commands that take no argument; anything after one is a mistake.

path-command.comment: Commands that load, unload, allow, silence or save a mod or a command file, with every alias the binary registers for them (`/race` for /loadrace, `/mut` and `/mutation` for /loadskill, `/livecode` for /loadlive, `/silentmod` for /silencemod, and so on). The argument is a mod, file or directory name and runs to the end of the line: it may contain spaces (`/loadmod fake crowns.mod.gml`, `/load custom options`) and slashes (`/loadskin skins/fish-hawaiian/hawaiian`), and the extension is optional (`/loadmod teloader`, `/loadmod baldi.race`). /savemod takes two paths and gets one path token for both; nothing here splits arguments. `/wep` is registered as an alias of /loadwep by the /help table even though a chat_cmd_wep script also exists for the per-player starting weapon; the table wins.

chat-command.comment: Every other command the 100.034 binary answers to. /load runs any chat command, not only the loading ones, so all of these are legal in a command file even though no file in the corpus uses one. Includes the per-player variants the binary registers - `color`/`colour` bare or with 2-4, `gamepad` bare or 1-4, `cwep` and `bwep` bare or 1-4, and `pwep`, which has no numbered variants - and the handler-only names `getset`, `gml_impl`, `debugstack`, `rootdir` and the `gp*` gamepad tuning commands, which no documentation mentions but which the chat_cmd_<name> convention still makes reachable.

unknown-command.comment: A slash word that is in none of the tables above - a typo, or a command from a newer NTT than 100.034. Only the word is scoped; the rest of the line is left alone, since there is no telling what it should have been.
